operations.comment: ; iNES header: eight 16 KiB PRG units, no CHR ROM, mapper 2 and vertical mirroring. Character
; patterns therefore use CHR RAM at runtime. This physical header is not CPU-addressable PRG
; data.
; The first byte of this 16 KiB PRG bank is its mapper-bank identity. Save/restore wrappers read
; it at CPU $8000; mapper bank numbers correspond to physical 8 KiB pairs (2*n,2*n+1). This tag
; is data, not the bank entry instruction.
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT RenderSceneSprites
; Build the OAM shadow for the current scene. When the alternate sprite mode is active, use the
; eight-slot list instead. Otherwise draw the sorted actor lists in alternating order each
; frame, then the three auxiliary actors. Hide unused OAM entries at Y=$F4 unless the sprite
; writer wrapped the buffer.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT RenderEightSlotSprites
; Visit the eight entries in the slot-order list. Skip zero sprite selectors; load each slot's
; attributes and two coordinates, then append its metasprite. Fill the remaining OAM Y fields
; with $F4 so old sprites disappear.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT RenderSortedActors
; Draw the two sentinel-terminated actor-index lists in opposite order on alternating frames.
; Each actor supplies a sprite selector, attributes and two coordinates from parallel arrays.
; Alternating order spreads OAM priority between overlapping actors.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT RenderAuxiliaryActors
; Scan three auxiliary actor slots in reverse order, skipping zero selectors. Their coordinates
; and attributes use the same parallel-array layout as the main actors.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT RenderClockSprites
; When the flag is nonnegative, place five sprites along the top edge. Four timer digits from
; the clock array become tile numbers by doubling the digit and adding $EA; fixed X positions
; come from the adjacent table. Negative input takes the inline-dispatch path beyond this block.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ClockSpriteHorizontalPositions
; Four fixed horizontal sprite positions used with the decimal clock digits. Digit-to-tile
; conversion happens in the reader; these bytes are positions, not character codes.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT DispatchClockVariant
; Mask the signed clock-sprite mode to its low nibble and tail-dispatch through the four
; currently bounded inline targets. DispatchInlineWordTable consumes the JSR return address, so
; the following words are payload. The accepted targets choose fixed or actor-relative OAM
; arrangements; arbitrary selector values beyond the established table prefix remain
; unsupported.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; 4 little-endian CPU target words consumed by DispatchInlineWordTable. The preceding JSR
; supplies the inline table base: the dispatcher removes that return address, doubles the
; selector and jumps through the selected word. These bytes are never the ordinary JSR
; continuation. Targets use the caller's current bank plus the fixed window. The next
; independently accepted handler bounds this slice; no complete original selector domain is
; implied beyond the checked entries.
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT WriteEightFixedClockSprites
; Fill the first eight OAM records with Y=$14, tile $FE, attributes zero and X=$10, working
; backward in four-byte steps. Return X=$20 so subsequent renderers append after this reserved
; group. The exact visual meaning of this fixed arrangement is unresolved.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT WriteActorRelativeClockSprites
; Two entries choose one of two eight-tile sets. Frame-counter bit four alternates the looked-up
; tiles with hidden tile $FE. Use actor-zero screen Y clamped to at least $40 minus $30, and
; actor-zero X plus per-sprite offsets. Write eight palette-three OAM records backward, then
; return X=$20 for later sprites. This is an actor-following blinking group, not the decimal
; timer rendering path.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ActorRelativeBlinkTilesAndOffsets
; Two eight-tile sets followed by per-sprite horizontal offsets. The reader blinks eight actor-
; relative OAM records using frame bit four; these are separate from decimal clock digits.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT WriteSingleFixedClockSprite
; Reserve one OAM record at Y/X=$10 with tile four and attributes $20. Return X=4 so subsequent
; OAM appends follow it. Its specific image identity is unresolved.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT AppendActorMetasprite
; A selects a little-endian pointer from the table at $8316. Each record begins with a component
; count, followed by Y offset, tile, attributes and X offset per sprite. Add the actor
; coordinates, merge its attribute flags and reflect horizontal offsets when requested. Reject
; wrapped X results; append four-byte OAM records until the component count expires or the OAM
; index wraps. The $06 flag controls a special attribute-bit path. Restore the caller's X index;
; the OAM cursor and wrap flag are outputs.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT SortActorDrawLists
; Partition active actors 12..0 by the sign of their X coordinate into two index lists
; terminated by $FF. Sort each list with adjacent swaps using the Y-coordinate array. This
; supplies depth ordering to the alternating-list renderer; scratch counters are local to the
; sort.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT AppendSlotMetasprite
; A indexes the pointer table at $83F6. Expand count-prefixed four-byte sprite components into
; OAM, adding coordinates and combining palette/flip flags. A component attribute bit chooses
; whether slot attributes are merged. Reflect horizontal offsets and reject coordinate wrap.
; Unlike the actor writer, this path does not test OAM-cursor wrap; callers must bound output.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; Actor and slot sprite selectors index little-endian CPU pointers, followed by 142 adjacent
; component records. Each record is a count and that many four-byte Y-offset, tile, attribute,
; X-offset components; the two renderers add actor coordinates and merge flip/palette flags.
; Selector zero in the first table aliases the genuine BCC instruction immediately before this
; data. The first independently bounded record begins at physical $00047A. Pointers are CPU
; addresses in bank zero; this is sprite data, including the bytes formerly decoded as
; undocumented instructions.
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ScanControlledActorContactWindow
; Unless the shared contact gate is set, select one team's controlled actor on alternating
; frames. Require an active sprite, nonnegative contact flags and state below four. Scan other
; actors against a rectangular screen-coordinate window, clearing their contact bit when
; outside. If no candidate remains, clear the controlled actor's contact bit as well. A
; candidate inside the window enters the response selector; this screen-space test is separate
; from world collision masks.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT SelectControlledActorContactResponse
; Reject candidates with existing contact status or state at least four. Partition relative
; vertical position into four bands and combine with horizontal distance to select a response
; vector. Same-side, opposing and auxiliary actors use distinct paths. Team response flags and
; actor action bits can increase the saturating response counters. Track repeated contact with
; the same actor; after two occurrences try the paired-actor sequence and choose which actor
; receives the primary response. The exact gameplay contact category remains tentative, while
; the windows, masks and pair-state mechanics are explicit.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ResolveContactPairVelocity
; Play the selected actor's parity-based contact sound, then write its selected four-byte
; response velocity. If either actor action flag is nonzero request sound $12. Restore the
; original actor, rotate the response selector by four modulo eight and tail-call the same
; vector writer for the opposite response. The shared RTS is also the no-response join.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT MarkActorContact
; Set bit zero of the selected actor's contact/status byte. Other flag bits are preserved.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ApplyDefaultContactResponse
; Shift the shared accumulator to establish carry, supply response base zero and join the
; modulo-eight response-selector calculation. Carry is an input to that calculation, so this is
; not an unconditional constant-zero vector.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT RememberContactActor
; Remember Y as the candidate actor and reset its two-update counter before joining the shared
; contact path.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT MarkSelectedActorContact
; On the accepted branch, restore the original selected actor in Y and set its contact bit only
; if its entire contact/status byte was zero. A nonzero status bypasses this change.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ApplyTeamSideContactResponse
; Combine alternating team parity with the selected team-side bit and the contact response
; index. Read a remapped response from the side-dependent table, then tail-call the common four-
; byte vector writer. This uses a direction/response table, with exact tactical naming
; unresolved.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT PlaySelectedActorContactSound
; Restore the original selected actor in Y and call the sound-selection fragment. The adjoining
; parity-vector path selects the contact response before the common vector application.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ChooseParityContactVector
; Combine scratch parity with the shared side bit, shift into an eight-entry group and merge the
; response selector. Read the contact-vector lookup and join the common vector application. The
; earlier path has already constrained the scratch fields; this entry adds no bounds check.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT IncreaseActorXResponse
; Add $20 plus incoming carry to the X-indexed actor response counter and saturate at $FF on
; overflow. Return without changing actor selection; callers intentionally supply carry from the
; preceding condition.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT IncreaseActorYResponse
; Add $20 plus incoming carry to the Y-indexed actor response counter and saturate at $FF on
; overflow. This is the companion operation for the other actor in the contact pair; the
; increment is not a plain carry-independent addition.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT LookupResponseVector
; Multiply response selector A by four and copy the four-byte fixed-bank record into actor Y's
; signed horizontal and vertical velocity pairs. The record is two little-endian components. The
; adjacent shared RTS supplies the return; the table is now classified as signed component
; records, while exact velocity scale remains unresolved.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ContactHelperBoundary
; One entry returns immediately; the following entry calls an actor helper. These are separate
; control-flow fragments, not proof that the call follows the RTS at runtime.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT TryStartPairedActorSequence
; After the setup comparison, compare sums of the two velocity-high bytes after the sign-fold
; helper; unequal sums return immediately. Require the selected controlled opponent and an
; action flag. Constrain the world horizontal position to an interior interval, align both
; actors' vertical position, save paired actor IDs and clear team counters. Enter actor state
; four with velocities/animation cleared, then place the two actors on opposite horizontal
; offsets facing opposite directions. This probably initiates the fighting pair sequence.
; Rejection returns A=$FF with carry derived from the shared accumulator; successful setup uses
; the actor reset helper's A=0 return.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT PlayParityContactSound
; Choose sound selector $4F or $50 from the low bit of actor index Y, then invoke the protected
; bank-6 wrapper. The sound's audible identity is unresolved.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT FinishPairedActorContact
; Set the selected partner state high and initialize its mode with selector three. Clear the two
; shared contact bytes. If its timer is zero, retry the existing contact test; otherwise move
; partner Y into X and tail into the common actor-state setter. This is the continuation after
; the parity sound, not an unconditional new contact.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT InitializePairedActorState
; Set actor Y state to four, clear both signed velocity components, animation frame/delay and
; the auxiliary action-timer field. The pair initializer invokes this once for each actor after
; aligning their coordinates. A=0 on return is used by its caller.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT FoldSignedVelocityHighByte
; Leave nonnegative A unchanged; complement all bits of negative A and return. This is a ones-
; complement sign fold for comparing high-byte motion magnitudes, not a full two's-complement
; absolute-value operation.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ContactResponseAndVectorParameters
; Contact response mapping bytes and signed component pairs used by the adjacent contact/vector
; logic. The response selector and parity choose subgroups; the original response names and
; complete subgroup schema remain unresolved.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT HideAuxiliaryPair
; Clear two auxiliary sprite selectors, hiding those OAM actors on the next render pass.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT InitializePairedAuxiliaryMotion
; Initialize both auxiliary entries from parallel byte and two-byte tables: horizontal position,
; horizontal page, vertical position and two signed velocity pairs. Clear their active/motion
; flags. The payload tables supply side-specific starts; physical screen identities and original
; motion units remain unresolved.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT AuxiliaryMotionInitialValues
; Parallel side-specific starting horizontal low/page and vertical bytes, followed by signed
; horizontal/vertical velocity pairs. The same starts feed the boundary/bounce setup; original
; screen identity and velocity scale remain unresolved.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT InitializeAndBoundAuxiliaryMotion
; Visit both auxiliary entries, derive sprite visibility and flip flags from team/mode parity
; and load a per-entry table value. For active motion compare integer coordinate with $7E/$A6
; according to velocity sign. Boundary crossing negates both signed velocity pairs through the
; following borrow-preserving tail, producing the bounce before coordinate integration.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ReflectBothAuxiliaryVelocityComponents
; Finish negating the first signed two-byte velocity using the borrow from its low-byte
; subtraction, then negate the other component with a fresh SEC. Continue into auxiliary
; coordinate integration. The complete paired negate makes a boundary bounce; it does not merely
; flip the velocity high-byte sign.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT IntegrateAuxiliaryCoordinates
; Add two fixed-point velocity pairs into their corresponding position pairs with carry
; propagation. Subtract camera coordinates to obtain screen coordinates. A nonzero high-byte
; difference hides the sprite; otherwise publish its screen coordinates.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT HideAuxiliaryEntry
; Clear the selected auxiliary sprite selector when its coordinate is outside the visible page.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT DispatchControlledActorState
; Resolve the actor controlled by logical player X, save its index and dispatch its per-actor
; substate only when the shared mode byte permits. The following three-word inline table selects
; the accepted controlled-actor handlers and is payload rather than ordinary return code.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; 3 little-endian CPU target words consumed by DispatchInlineWordTable. The preceding JSR
; supplies the inline table base: the dispatcher removes that return address, doubles the
; selector and jumps through the selected word. These bytes are never the ordinary JSR
; continuation. Targets use the caller's current bank plus the fixed window. The next
; independently accepted handler bounds this slice; no complete original selector domain is
; implied beyond the checked entries.
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT StartTimedActorSubstate
; Choose a short control/action value from actor parity, player fields and the evolving byte
; accumulator. Seed an actor timer to $10..$13 and advance its substate. The accumulator is used
; as a pseudo-random selector here, but its distribution and gameplay intent are not
; established.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT TimedActorControlValues
; Three short action/control values selected from parity and evolving player/accumulator fields.
; The reader separately seeds a $10..$13 timer; these bytes are control values rather than timer
; lengths.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT WaitActorTimerThenSetAction
; Count down the actor timer. On expiry choose $44 or $48 from a bit of the evolving accumulator
; and store the resulting action/control byte. Other transitions lie outside the fragment.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ActorControlSharedReturn
; Return from the actor-control phase to its caller. Several timing/selector paths share this
; RTS; it is a join rather than an independent event handler.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT TickPlayerCounterEverySixteenFrames
; When the low four frame bits are zero, increment the current logical player's counter. The
; full counter purpose remains unresolved; continue into DispatchActorControlMode.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT WrapTeamAnimationCounter
; When the per-team counter reaches twenty, clear it and advance a second team counter modulo
; four. Restore X from the saved actor index before the next control step. Counters below twenty
; simply keep their current values; this is a bounded phase animation/control timer.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT DispatchActorControlMode
; Select one of four modes from the game gate, team parity and sign of a shared ownership/mode
; byte, then invoke the inline dispatcher. This establishes conditional control modes without
; identifying each target's game meaning.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; 4 little-endian CPU target words consumed by DispatchInlineWordTable. The preceding JSR
; supplies the inline table base: the dispatcher removes that return address, doubles the
; selector and jumps through the selected word. These bytes are never the ordinary JSR
; continuation. Targets use the caller's current bank plus the fixed window. The next
; independently accepted handler bounds this slice; no complete original selector domain is
; implied beyond the checked entries.
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ChooseActorActionDelayFromTeamPhase
; Combine shared mode, team-sign flag and a frame/phase counter into a delay-table selector.
; Increment the actor timer and compare with the selected threshold. Before expiry return
; unchanged; at expiry clear the timer and set action byte $80. The table mechanics are
; established while the exact gameplay action name remains uncertain.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ActorPhaseDelayThresholds
; Delay thresholds selected from shared mode, team sign and phase, with a small comparison group
; at the end. Expiry triggers action $80. Complete original selector semantics remain
; unresolved.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT DispatchActorTeamControlPhase
; On frame-counter zero increment the selected team's phase counter, then restore actor X.
; Update its team-direction/control helper and dispatch actor substate through the two bounded
; inline target words. Frame wrap is a byte wrap, not a once-per-second clock.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; Two little-endian CPU target words consumed by DispatchInlineWordTable. The preceding JSR
; supplies the table base; its return address is removed and the selected word is jumped
; through. The words select the initialization and sustained actor chase handlers. They are
; inline payload rather than ordinary return code; the independently checked extent does not
; imply arbitrary selector values are valid.
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT InitializeActorChasePhase
; Load a team-dependent actor action/target record and refresh directional response. Clear the
; team response flag, initialize a short steering limit and timer, advance actor substate and
; clear its action byte. This supplies the setup for the following sustained chase/target
; handler.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT UpdateActorChaseAndAction
; For a negative scripted response, compare its low-nibble phase with the shared input phase and
; either consume it or steer toward a center target. Otherwise count down response delay,
; inspect action flags and team conditions, and choose special action $80/$40 or refresh the
; target behavior. Steering uses bounded proximity tests and movement toward stored target. Non-
; action actors target a side-specific offset from the parity reference actor; action actors
; retain their target unless the local direction helper changes it. Timers and a short steering-
; count field limit updates. These mechanics plausibly form computer-controlled play, without
; assigning original tactic names.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ActorChaseTargetOffsets
; Side-specific target offsets consumed by actor chase/action steering. The reference actor
; supplies the origin; these bytes refine the target rather than encode execution addresses.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ChooseOpponentControlledActorAsTarget
; If the selected team has an enabled response flag, the shared phase is below eight and the
; team response is pending, copy the opposing controlled actor's world coordinates into this
; actor's stored target and return carry set. Otherwise clear the pending team response and
; return carry clear. X remains the moving actor; Y is scratch for team/candidate selection.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT TestTimedOpposingActorWindow
; Increment a per-team counter and, at its mode-dependent threshold, reset it and return carry
; clear. Otherwise project a small screen-coordinate window from the actor's eight-way direction
; and scan active opposite-parity actors. Return carry set when both unsigned coordinate deltas
; are below $28; otherwise clear after the scan. This is a local avoidance/action window, not
; the world-mask collision test.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT OpposingActorWindowParameters
; Mode-dependent counter limits and paired direction offsets used to project the local opposite-
; team search window. Successful coordinate deltas must each be below $28; original tactical
; naming remains uncertain.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT TurnActorForNearbyOpponent
; For nonzero shared mode project a direction-dependent screen window and scan opposite-parity
; actors. If none is inside, return carry clear. For a hit choose turn sign using the actor's
; vertical half, direction and facing; apply the mode-dependent direction adjustment through the
; circular steering helper, set timer $18 and return carry set. This is a bounded local turn
; response; exact tactics remain unresolved.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ActorSteeringPhaseAndTargetParameters
; Steering/turn offsets, phase values and fixed target coordinates used by the adjacent actor
; control routines. Reader-associated subgroups are established; unconsumed patterned remainder
; has no recovered complete schema.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT LoadTeamActorResponseRecord
; Choose a response-table pointer from the team selector, then combine an action-dependent phase
; and masked shared accumulator to index a two-byte record. Store its response and delay to the
; actor. Derive action flags from the response high nibble; the high-bit case enters a separate
; team phase update. This is a record consumer, not a proof of the full table domain.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT LoadPhaseActorTarget
; Use the shared phase to select a target vertical coordinate and a side-dependent two-byte
; horizontal target. Save all three actor target fields and return. Target selection uses the
; actor facing flag; no specific rink/tactical landmark is claimed.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT AdvanceTeamResponseAndCenterTarget
; Advance the team response counter modulo eight, combine it with shared mode and load a team
; response field. Restore actor X and set its target to fixed world coordinates Y=$96, X=$01A0.
; This is the response-mode center target used by the sustained chase handler.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT TeamResponseCycleValues
; Team response values indexed by shared mode and a counter modulo eight. The reader then
; targets fixed world center $01A0/$96. These are response-state parameters, not coordinates
; themselves.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT CompareActorWithStoredTargetWindow
; Accept A as a component-distance threshold. Compute absolute vertical difference and a two-
; byte absolute horizontal difference from the actor's stored target. Return carry clear only
; when both are strictly below the threshold and horizontal high difference is zero; equality or
; a larger component returns carry set. This rectangular test is distinct from scaled squared
; distance.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT UpdateActorResponseFromOpponentPositions
; Only for shared phase values two/three, compare same-side facing and horizontal ordering of
; opposite-parity actors. Count those on the selected side of the current actor; when fewer than
; three, set response $80 and a one-update timer. Other phases leave state intact. The
; comparator follows the original byte ordering and facing masks; no exact tactical purpose is
; assigned.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ComputeActorFieldPositionPhase
; Compare the actor's two-byte horizontal position against seven thresholds. Reflect the
; horizontal bin when facing is nonzero, clamp it to five and double it. Add the vertical-half
; bit from comparison with $96, then XOR a per-team alternating phase bit and save the result in
; $17. This builds a field-position/control-table phase; original tactical bin names are
; unresolved.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ActorFieldHorizontalThresholds
; Little-endian horizontal threshold words used to divide actor position into bins. The reader
; reflects by facing, clamps the bin and adds a vertical-half/alternating phase bit; original
; tactical bin names remain unresolved.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT DispatchActorSupportSubstate
; Tail-dispatch actor substate through the adjacent two-word inline table. The shared dispatcher
; consumes the return address; the payload selects setup versus sustained support/target
; processing.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; 2 little-endian CPU target words consumed by DispatchInlineWordTable. The preceding JSR
; supplies the inline table base: the dispatcher removes that return address, doubles the
; selector and jumps through the selected word. These bytes are never the ordinary JSR
; continuation. Targets use the caller's current bank plus the fixed window. The next
; independently accepted handler bounds this slice; no complete original selector domain is
; implied beyond the checked entries.
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT InitializeActorSupportPhase
; Initialize the actor timer to one, advance its substate and clear the action byte. This
; provides a one-update entry delay before the sustained support handler.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT UpdateActorSupportTarget
; Require the actor-target predicate, then handle a signed per-team throttle on alternating
; frames. While the team is active, positive throttle clears the actor action; its underflow
; reloads a negative cooldown. After the actor timer expires choose the next delay from shared
; mode, team phase and signed team comparison. Seek an opposite-parity category-zero actor: an
; action-flagged candidate becomes the direct target; otherwise choose the side-specific offset
; from the parity reference actor. Turn one step toward the resulting target. The local throttle
; and selection mechanics are established; a precise tactical role remains tentative.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ActorSupportDelayAndOffsets
; Mode/team-dependent support delays plus side-specific target offsets and throttle comparisons.
; The support reader combines these with a parity reference actor; complete tactical
; interpretation remains tentative.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ChaseSharedObjectWithTeamThrottle
; Require the same local target predicate. A nonzero team throttle decrements and forces action
; zero. Otherwise copy shared-object coordinates into the actor target, steer one direction step
; and update its timer through a mode-dependent mask. At timer zero and with inactive team
; state, add action bit $40; the next accepted fragment stores it. This bounds action cadence
; without assigning an original tactic name.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT StoreActorAction
; Store the action/control byte in A to the actor indexed by X and return.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ActorChaseCadenceMasks
; Mode-indexed timer masks controlling chase/action cadence. The reader adds action bit $40 only
; at the resulting zero timer under its team-state gate.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT TestActorTargetWindow
; Selector zero bypasses the cadence read and opposing-actor state test. Selectors one/two AND
; 64/32-frame masks with FrameCounter; only zero results test the opposing controlled actor for
; state two and branch to direction selection on a match. Otherwise select a bounds window. Compare vertical
; position with a byte range and two-byte horizontal position with paired bounds. Reject through
; carry-clear paths; the now-classified inside tail returns carry set. Exact tactical window
; naming remains tentative.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ActorTargetCheckCadenceMasks
; Selector one/two masks gate the opposing-controlled-actor state-two test every 64/32
; frames; the bounds-window test still runs on other frames. Selector zero bypasses this read; its dummy base is the
; preceding RTS at $9C6E, which remains code. Menu adjustment bounds the selector to
; zero through two, but this does not prove every caller's domain or a natural read.
; Effective PRG banks 0/1/14/15; the physical table begins at $1C7F (CPU $9C6F).
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ChooseDirectionTowardParityActor
; Select actor 10 or 11 by parity. Compare its coordinate against the shared target, choosing
; vertical direction bits $04/$08 and horizontal bits $01/$02. Store the combined action to the
; current actor. A shared motion flag suppresses the horizontal comparison.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ActorTargetPredicateTrue
; Shared predicate return with carry set. Its callers interpret acceptance according to their
; own actor-target/action checks.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT ActorTargetWindowBounds
; Byte vertical limits followed by paired low/high horizontal bounds. Ownership/direction choose
; one of two local target windows; these values constrain positions rather than identify actors.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT DispatchAlternatingTeamControl
; If the shared mode is zero, return. Otherwise select a team by frame parity, update it and
; join a second helper. The inner dispatcher compares team parity to the ownership byte and
; chooses one of two inline targets.
; END REVIEWED UNIT
; 2 little-endian CPU target words consumed by DispatchInlineWordTable. The preceding JSR
; supplies the inline table base: the dispatcher removes that return address, doubles the
; selector and jumps through the selected word. These bytes are never the ordinary JSR
; continuation. Targets use the caller's current bank plus the fixed window. The next
; independently accepted handler bounds this slice; no complete original selector domain is
; implied beyond the checked entries.
; BEGIN REVIEWED UNIT UpdateTeamControlAtTwoCadences
; Two entries call the shared target-candidate refresher, then supply masks $F0 or $FE to the
